Kitchen Remodeling in Derby, KS

Derby's housing stock tells the story of south Sedgwick County's growth: 1960s and 1970s ranches in the older neighborhoods near Rock Road and Madison, and newer 1990s–2000s builds in the subdivisions that expanded Derby into one of the metro's larger suburbs. Both eras present distinct kitchen problems — and both are well past the point where a coat of paint and new hardware are going to fix anything.

The older Derby ranches have original galley kitchens that were never intended to be social spaces. Closed off from the living areas, narrow, and equipped with cabinets that have survived 50+ years of Kansas humidity cycles but aren't going to survive another decade. The newer builds have builder-grade kitchens that looked fine at move-in and have been slowly deteriorating since — particle-board cabinet boxes, laminate countertops at the end of their seal life, and ventilation that moves air but doesn't actually clear steam and cooking odors.

Wheatland Construction remodels both. We're a Veterans Approved Builder (ID: 00899), Home Advisor Certified since 2019, and family-owned since 2018. Derby is a regular part of our work area — we know the housing stock here.

What Derby Homeowners Most Often Need

The most common kitchen remodel scenarios we see in Derby:

Older 1960s–1970s homes near Rock Road corridor: Full gut renovations — new layout, open-concept conversion, new cabinets and countertops, updated plumbing and electrical, proper exterior-vented range hood, new flooring. These kitchens haven't been seriously touched in decades and they need it. The good news is the bones are often solid — these homes were built with real wood framing — and the transformation is dramatic.

1990s–2000s subdivisions east of K-15: Mid-range refreshes — cabinet replacement or refacing depending on box condition, countertop upgrade to quartz, new backsplash, lighting update, open-concept wall removal if the layout calls for it. These kitchens don't need a gut — they need honest materials replacing the builder-grade originals that have reached end of life.

Kitchen-to-living-area openings: One of the most-requested projects in Derby across both housing vintages. We assess whether the wall is load-bearing, quote the structural work, handle the beam installation and permit, and coordinate the flooring transition so the whole space feels intentional rather than patched.

Our Remodeling Process in Derby

Free in-home consultation, honest scope and pricing, permits through the City of Derby Community Development department, our own crews for demo and build. We assess plumbing, electrical, and structural conditions before finalizing the estimate. Timeline is typically 6–10 weeks from permit issuance.

How We Approach Kitchen Remodeling in Derby

Every kitchen remodel starts with a site visit. We measure the existing layout, look at the plumbing rough-in and drain stack location, check the electrical panel for capacity, and assess structural walls before discussing what's possible. We price in writing with every line item documented.

Our crew handles demo through final walkthrough. Cabinet delivery, tile setting, countertop templating, plumbing trim-out, electrical, and final inspection all coordinated through us - no handoffs to subcontractors who don't know the project.

Wheatland Construction has held Veterans Approved Builder status (ID: 00899) since we opened and has been Home Advisor Certified since 2019. We're licensed and insured in Kansas.

In Derby, Sedgwick County's fastest-growing suburb, renovation ROI is strong across all housing vintages - from 1960s originals to 2000s production builds.

Frequently Asked Questions About Kitchen Remodeling in Derby

How much does kitchen remodeling cost in Derby, KS?

Derby kitchen remodels range from $20,000 for a mid-range refresh to $70,000+ for a full gut renovation with structural work and high-end finishes. Open-concept conversions in Derby's 1990s ranch homes typically run $30,000–$55,000 all-in. Written, line-item estimates on every project.

Do I need permits for kitchen remodeling in Derby?

Yes — plumbing, electrical, and structural work (including wall removal) requires permits through the City of Derby Community Development. We handle all permit applications, fees, and inspections.

How long does a kitchen remodel take in Derby?

6–10 weeks from permit issuance for most projects. Full gut renovations with structural changes may run 10–14 weeks. We give you a realistic schedule at the start and communicate throughout.

Can you remove the wall between my Derby kitchen and living room?

Usually yes — we assess structural status first. Most 1960s–1970s Derby ranch homes have identifiable structural patterns; we check before committing. We quote the structural work, beam installation, and permit as part of the total scope.

What kitchen materials hold up best in south Sedgwick County's climate?

Quartz countertops outperform granite and natural stone for maintenance in Kansas kitchens — they don't require sealing and hold up to humidity swings. Plywood-box cabinets with solid wood door fronts outperform particle-board or MDF. LVP flooring is the practical choice for kitchen and adjacent open-concept areas — durable, waterproof, and comfortable underfoot.

Do you serve all of Derby or just certain areas?

All of Derby — older neighborhoods near downtown and Rock Road, newer subdivisions off 71st Street and K-15, and everything in between.
